precepts.text: The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire. That pillar of cloud is a chariot, and the Lord was inside it: that is the Rock that followed them. He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night.
precepts.point: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen: there remained not so much as one of them. Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore. And the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses. We celebrated Passover.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
In Exodus 14:19-20 “the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these”. Who was in that pillar? Exodus 13:21 says it: “And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night”.

Who went before them in the pillar of cloud? Christ. That pillar of cloud is a chariot, and the Lord was inside it. It is the Rock that followed them in 1 Corinthians 10. Imagine seeing something bright, what you would call a UFO today, come down and stand between you and your enemy. The Egyptians saw that, and you know they were afraid.

“He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.” Day and night it was with them. And it was through that same “pillar of fire and of the cloud” that the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians in the morning watch, troubled them and took off their chariot wheels, until they said “Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”

precepts.text: How long shall I bear with this evil congregation? When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: liars, fornicators, murmurers. Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness, from twenty years old and upward. Once you were 20 years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Even Aaron died, and Moses did not enter; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger. Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it into the promised land. Everybody 20 and up, their blood was on their own head, because according to the law, at 20 you are the age of a man and you take responsibility for yourself. The little ones which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in. The children wandered 40 years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, until every last rebellious one died. That is what the Lord did to us in the wilderness: he purged that leaven out of our people.
precepts.point: It shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord's law may be in thy mouth. Why are we celebrating the days of unleavened bread? It is a sign for us to keep God's laws, for God's laws to be in our minds. That is what the days of unleavened bread really represent.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
Exodus 13:8 says “And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This is done means the feast of unleavened bread. But what did the Lord do unto me? The Lord delivered everyone, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. Numbers 14 shows what he did.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators, murmurers. The Lord said, “as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”. Once you were twenty years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Aaron died. Moses died too; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger, so he did not see the promised land, though when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it in. According to the law, at twenty you are the age of a man and take responsibility for yourself, which is why twenty is the age to marry. Everybody twenty and up, their blood was on their own head.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The children wandered forty years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, seeing all the evil they did, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness”: until every last one of those wicked Israelites died, everybody who had leaven in them, the murmurers, the adulterers, the ones who held on to Egypt.

So the me of Exodus 13:8 is not Moses. It is the little ones, twenty years and under, who grew up in the land and told their sons: we keep unleavened bread because the Lord purged the leaven out of me in the wilderness. And it is the same in the future: whoever keeps leaven, which is sin, through the seven days, that soul shall be cut off.

precepts.text: This day came ye out in the month Abib. Abib is the first month of the ancient Hebrew calendar, corresponding to parts of March and April; the word literally means ear of grain, when the barley is ripe but still soft, marking the start of the spring harvest. So when you see Israelites celebrating Passover in the winter, they do not know what they are talking about. They changed the new year from spring to the dead of winter; that is what God is warning us about in Daniel 7:25.
precepts.point: And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time: time is singular, times is plural, and the dividing is the half; that is three and a half, as Revelation explains.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Which month did God make the beginning of months? “This day came ye out in the month Abib.” Abib is the name of the first month of the ancient Hebrew calendar, generally corresponding to parts of March and April in the modern Gregorian calendar: the end of March into the beginning of April, the spring season.

The word comes from Hebrew and literally means ear of grain, young green ears, sprouting. It refers to the stage when barley is ripe but still soft, marking the start of the spring harvest. God's new year begins in spring, when the barley comes in.

So when you see Israelites celebrating Passover in the winter, they don't know what the hell they are talking about. The new year was changed from spring to the dead of winter. That is what God warns us about in Daniel 7:25: he shall “think to change times and laws”.

precepts.text: Remember this day in which ye came out from Egypt.
precepts.point: January is not the new year.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
In Egypt the Lord told Moses and Aaron, “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you”. Jump to verse 11 to see what holiday comes in that month: “ye shall eat it in haste: it is the Lord’s passover”. So Passover comes in the first month. But what is the name of that first month?

Exodus 13 tells us: “And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten. This day came ye out in the month Abib”.

Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear. It marks the start of the year, the time of Passover and the firstfruits, renewal and freedom from Egypt. So the first month, the month of Passover, is the spring month. Not January.

That matters, because the months of the year are all from Rome. January is named for Janus, the Roman god of beginnings, and America, exercising all the power of the first beast, has the whole earth keeping Rome's new year. The Most High set the beginning of months in the spring, the month we came out of the house of bondage.

precepts.text: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel to carry his bones away with them.
precepts.point: That is why no Egyptologist can show you the mummy of Joseph, the tomb of so famous a man: when Israel fled out of the land of Egypt they took the bones of Joseph with them, according to that oath.

note.label: Genesis 50: The Burial of Jacob and the Forgiveness of Joseph

precepts.why:
Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel before he died: “God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.” They embalmed him and “he was put in a coffin in Egypt.” Exodus shows that oath being kept. When Israel went out of Egypt, “Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.”

That is why no Egyptologist can show you the mummy of Joseph, the tomb of so famous a man. Joseph lived an hundred and ten years in Egypt, saw Ephraim’s children of the third generation and had the children of Machir the son of Manasseh brought up upon his knees, yet his body is not in Egypt. When Israel fled out of the land they took the bones of Joseph with them, according to that oath.

precepts.text: This day came ye out in the month Abib; the exodus month is the first month of the year.
precepts.point: Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter; that is another lie taught in Babylon.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

precepts.why:
“This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” Which month is it? Moses names it: “This day came ye out in the month Abib.” The month Israel came out of Egypt is Abib, and Abib is the first month of the year.

Abib in the Bible dictionary is the pre-exilic name for the first month of the year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan, and it falls between March and April. So the new year begins in the springtime, around March and April, not on January the first in the dead of winter. That is another lie taught in Babylon. The year the Most High gave Israel begins with the month he brought them out.

precepts.text: We remember the fish, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick; the people longed for Egypt in the wilderness.
precepts.point: So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

precepts.why:
God led Israel around the land of the Philistines, “Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt”. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back, because the people felt a false security in Egypt.

That false security shows itself in the wilderness. “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. Out of bondage, they murmured for the food of Egypt: the fish, the leeks, the onions and the garlick. Egypt had fed them, and they longed for it.

The same spirit holds the people in America today: a little job, government assistance, a car, food from the store, and they never want this kingdom to come down. The Lord knew that spirit when he chose the road out of Egypt, and led the people about through the wilderness of the Red sea so they would not run back.

precepts.text: Our soul loatheth this light bread; the murmuring shows the false comfort Israel took in Egypt.
precepts.point: So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

precepts.why:
“And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.” The Lord fed them from heaven, and they loathed it, and asked why they were ever brought up out of Egypt.

That murmuring shows the false comfort Israel took in Egypt. At the first hardship they looked back. That is exactly why God said “Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt” and led them the long way: a people who loathe the light bread and miss Egypt for its food would have turned back at the first sight of the Philistines.

The same spirit is in the people in America today, holding on to a little job, government assistance, a car and food from the store, never wanting this kingdom to come down.

precepts.text: Woe to the rebellious children that walk to go down into Egypt to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh; Israel kept running back to Egypt for safety.
precepts.point: So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

precepts.why:
Israel never stopped running back to Egypt. When the Assyrians came, Israel ran down to Egypt for help, and the Lord called it rebellion: “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!”

To strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh and trust in the shadow of Egypt: that is the false security God saw in the people when he led them around the way of the Philistines, lest they see war and return to Egypt. The spirit that would have turned them back at the sight of war took them down to Egypt again in the days of the Assyrians, without asking at his mouth. And it holds the people in America today, trusting in the shadow of this kingdom and never wanting it to come down.

precepts.text: In my Father's house are many mansions; the Most High has something far greater in store than the false security of this captivity.
precepts.point: So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

precepts.why:
Against the false security of Egypt, the Most High has something much greater in store. Christ says, “In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.”

A little job, government assistance, a car and food from the store are the fish and the leeks of Egypt. What is prepared for Israel is the world, the earth, and many mansions in the Father's house. God led the people about through the wilderness so they would not trade that for Egypt, and the people in America who never want this kingdom to come down are holding on to Egypt when the Most High has far more in store for them.

precepts.text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel; that was the office before the Levites were taken instead.
precepts.point: The Levites were given as a gift to Aaron and to his sons, to do the service of the children of Israel and to make an atonement for them, that there be no plague among the children of Israel when they come nigh unto the sanctuary.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
Mark the word instead in verse 16: the Levites were taken “instead of such as open every womb, even instead of the firstborn of all the children of Israel.” At the first, the office belonged to all the firstborn of all the tribes. “And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.”

The firstborn were sanctified for the office from the day the Lord smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt. Here he makes it clear again, as he has done in multiple places, that the one tribe of Levi now performs the service of the tabernacle instead of them, given as a gift to Aaron and his sons to make an atonement for the children of Israel, that there be no plague when they come nigh unto the sanctuary.

precepts.text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn: the firstling is the glory of the birthright.
precepts.point: And they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh: the blessing on Jacob's grandsons was to grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. The Most High gets geographic with it: they went from the east to the west and multiplied in the midst of the hemisphere, in Central America.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“His glory is like the firstling of his bullock”. The firstling is the firstborn, and the law sanctified the firstborn unto the Most High: “Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.”

That is the glory of the birthright given to Joseph. The firstling belongs to the Most High, and Joseph's glory is like the firstling of his bullock, the portion of the firstborn.
